1. Get started and find your way

Learn the screen areas, organise your work, and practise the gestures you will use most often.

The workspace

chicCanva is organised like a worktable: projects and quick commands are at the top, the page is in the centre, and tools with their settings are in the side panel.

Where to find it: The whole main screen. Open panel or Close panel shows and hides the side column.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Project stripSwitch between separate pieces of work and create a new project.When preparing different resources without mixing them.
ToolbarSelection, zoom, copy, layers, crop, and other immediate commands.For frequent actions on an object or the view.
PageShows the active page and the objects that will be exported.This is where you compose the resource.
Side panelCollects features and settings in collapsible sections.Open it to choose or adjust a tool; close it for more space.

How to use it

  1. Open the panel and notice the quick links: Page, Text, Fonts, Emoji, Shapes, Images, Colorizer, Clipart, AI, and Export.
  2. Select a link: the matching section opens and is brought into view.
  3. Keep Expand one at a time enabled if you prefer one section at a time; disable it to compare several sections.
  4. Scroll bars horizontally when there are more commands than fit on screen.
Recommended choices

If you cannot find a command, start from the panel’s quick links. Icons show a tooltip on hover; on touch, use this guide or the explanation inside the section.

Guided example
Your first tour
Goal
Find where to create text and where to export it.
Steps
  1. Open Text and type TEST.
  2. Choose Add text and look at the page.
  3. Open Export and inspect the available choices without exporting.
Expected result
A page with text and a mental map of the two panels used.
Try next
Open Fonts and change typeface, then return to Text using the quick link.
Continue with:Projects and pagesAdding textExporting

Projects and pages

A project is one complete piece of work; it can contain one or many pages. Each page can have its own size, orientation, and name.

Where to find it: Project tabs above the canvas and the Page management section in the panel.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
+ ProjectOpens a separate new piece of work.To keep classes, activities, or versions separate.
+ PageAdds a page after the active one.For booklets, sequences, flashcards, and multi-page resources.
DuplicateCreates a matching page to edit.When you want to retain layout and style.
A4, A3, A5, Letter, Square, CustomSet the physical page size.A4 for worksheets, A3 for posters, Square for digital cards, Custom for special sizes.
Before / AfterReorders the page without precise dragging.Especially useful on phones and tablets.

How to use it

  1. Choose + Project, give it a recognisable name, and confirm.
  2. In Page management, choose size and orientation.
  3. Add or duplicate the pages you need and give them useful names, such as Cover, Activity 1, Answers.
  4. Use numbered chips, Before/After, or Preview to change page and order.
Recommended choices

Portrait A4 is a good starting point for a worksheet. Use landscape A3 for a poster. Long names are shortened only on screen: the full name remains saved.

Guided example
A three-page booklet
Goal
Prepare a cover, activity, and answer page in one project.
Steps
  1. Create a project called Numbers to 10.
  2. Rename the first page Cover.
  3. Duplicate it twice and name the copies Activity and Answers.
  4. Use Before/After to check the order.
Expected result
Three ordered pages, ready for different content with the same size.
Try next
Open Preview and compare the set before exporting to PDF.
Continue with:Preview and reorderSaving and recovery

Zoom, Fit, hand tool, and pinch

These commands only change how you view the page. They do not enlarge objects or change print quality.

Where to find it: Toolbar above the page; on touch devices you can also use two fingers.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
FitShows the whole page in the available space.To review the whole composition.
Percentage / + / −Zooms the view in or out.For working on small details.
Hand toolDrags the workspace without moving objects.When highly zoomed in.
Ctrl + wheelZooms around the pointer.For quick adjustment with a mouse or trackpad.
Two-finger pinchZooms and pans the view at the same time.On a phone, tablet, or touch screen.

How to use it

  1. Choose Fit to begin with the whole page.
  2. Zoom in on the detail you want to adjust.
  3. Enable the hand tool or use two fingers to bring that detail to the centre.
  4. Return to selection with V when you want to edit objects.
Recommended choices

During a pinch, objects and active tools are suspended: both fingers are used only for navigation. The previous selection returns when the gesture ends.

Guided example
Refine one letter
Goal
Correct a small alignment detail without losing the overall view.
Steps
  1. Choose Fit and locate the letter.
  2. Set zoom to 200%.
  3. Use the hand tool to centre it and make the correction.
  4. Return to Fit to check the result.
Expected result
The detail is corrected and the overall layout is unchanged.
Try next
Use Preview to check the same position on duplicated pages.
Continue with:Selecting and transformingUsing mobile

Select, move, and transform

Before editing an element, select it. The boundary and handles show what will be moved, resized, rotated, copied, or deleted.

Where to find it: Selection icon in the toolbar and the object context menu.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Click or tapSelects one object.For a direct edit.
Selection rectangleCollects objects inside an area.For nearby objects that do not overlap.
Ctrl + clickAdds or removes items from the selection.On desktop, for precise choices.
Tap selectionBuilds a selection with successive taps without dragging.On touch devices or with overlapping objects.
Lock proportionsKeeps the width-to-height ratio while resizing.For images, logos, and compositions that must not distort.
Lock positionPrevents accidental movement.For backgrounds and finished elements.

How to use it

  1. Enable Select or press V.
  2. Select the object; use Ctrl, the rectangle, or Tap selection for several objects.
  3. Drag inside to move, the corners to resize, and the top handle to rotate when Rotate is enabled.
  4. Press Escape during the gesture to return to the starting position.
Recommended choices

For images and groups, normally use corner handles. Shift temporarily reverses the proportion lock. Arrow keys move by 1 pixel; Shift + arrow moves by 10 pixels.

Guided example
Align a title and decorations
Goal
Move a title and two stars together without changing their arrangement.
Steps
  1. Start Tap selection.
  2. Tap the title and both stars.
  3. Finish the mode and drag the selection.
  4. Group it if you will move it again.
Expected result
The three items move together while preserving their spacing.
Try next
Use Fit with margin to centre the group on the page.
Continue with:Groups and layersGrid and alignment

Undo, saving, and recovery

chicCanva automatically keeps your work in the browser and records major edits. A JSON file is the copy to keep or move to another device.

Where to find it: Undo/Redo controls in the top bar; Memory section; Export centre for JSON.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Undo / RedoMoves back or reapplies a change.After unwanted movement, styling, cropping, or deletion.
HistoryShows several reachable states.With right-click or long press on Undo/Redo.
AutosaveLets you resume work in the same browser.Keep it enabled during normal sessions.
Export JSONSaves the editable project to a file.At the end of an important session or to transfer work.
JSON with historyAlso includes Undo/Redo states.When the recipient needs previous states; it is larger.

How to use it

  1. Keep autosave enabled.
  2. Use Undo as soon as you notice an incorrect change.
  3. Periodically export JSON with a recognisable name and date.
  4. When reopening, choose Resume project if chicCanva finds previous work.
Recommended choices

Autosave protects against refreshes but belongs to that browser and address. JSON is the portable backup. PDF and PNG are for using or printing the result, not editing it.

Guided example
Finish a session safely
Goal
Keep both the editable project and the ready-to-use resource.
Steps
  1. Review pages in Preview.
  2. Export the JSON.
  3. Also export the final PDF or images.
  4. Check that the files are in Downloads.
Expected result
You have one copy for continued editing and one for printing or sharing.
Try next
Add a date or version to the JSON filename to keep several milestones.
Continue with:Choosing an export formatReviewing all pages
✏️

2. Create with text, symbols, and shapes

Build headings, worksheets, and decorations while keeping every element editable.

Add and edit text

Text can be one phrase or a composition of separate letters and groups. You can correct it later without recreating it.

Where to find it: Add text section; when text is selected, Edit text object appears.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
ALL UPPERCASEConverts new content to uppercase.Headings, cut-out letters, and posters.
One object per letter / groupSeparates content so parts can be coloured or moved.Banners, alphabets, syllables, and creative lettering.
Smart EmojiTurns Unicode emoji into graphical OpenMoji.For crisp, printable emoji that can be edited separately.
Contain / Width / HeightAutomatically fits new text to the page.Contain is safest; Width for headings; Height for large letters.
Keep width / heightDuring editing, keeps the occupied space.When replacing a word without changing the layout.

How to use it

•Text→•Type the phrase→•Add text→Fit page
  1. Type the phrase in the large field.
  2. Choose uppercase, Smart Emoji, and fitting mode.
  3. Choose Add text.
  4. To correct it, select the text, open Edit text object, change the content, and choose which dimensions to keep.
Recommended choices

For a normal phrase, use one object: it is easier to align. If each letter needs a different colour, create separate objects or use Split text after choosing font and size.

Guided example
Rainbow heading
Goal
Create a heading with differently coloured letters.
Steps
  1. Type WELCOME and choose One object per letter.
  2. Choose Add text.
  3. Select each letter and change its colour.
  4. Group all letters when the composition is ready.
Expected result
A cheerful heading that remains editable letter by letter.
Try next
Add two OpenMoji at the sides and include them in the group.
Continue with:Choosing a fontFill and outlineGrouping

Split text and one letter per page

Split divides finished text; Special Functions and Projects automatically creates one page for each letter or group.

Where to find it: Scissors icon in the toolbar and Special Functions and Projects section.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Split textTurns text into separate parts while keeping appearance and position.After choosing font and size.
^ explicit groupsManually decides which letters stay together.For syllables, digraphs, or short words: WA^TER.
New projectCreates the banner without changing the open work.Recommended for a new activity.
Append pagesAdds results to the current project.When the cover and letters belong together.
Constant sizeUses the same scale on every page.For a visually even banner.

How to use it

  1. Enter the content and choose how symbols and apostrophes are joined.
  2. Choose orientation, fitting, and destination.
  3. Check the preview of the resulting groups.
  4. Generate the pages and open Preview to check order and consistency.
Recommended choices

For a banner, use landscape A4, constant size, and a new project. For syllable cards, use ^ to keep chosen groups together.

Guided example
WELCOME banner
Goal
Create one large, even letter on each page.
Steps
  1. Open Special Functions and Projects and type WELCOME.
  2. Choose New project, landscape A4, and Constant size.
  3. Generate and review pages in Preview.
  4. Export all pages as PDF.
Expected result
A print-ready PDF with one letter per sheet.
Try next
Create another version with different colours.
Continue with:Managing pagesExporting the banner

Choose a readable, suitable font

A font changes the visual character of a resource and can help or hinder reading. chicCanva offers direct search, categories, and a guided wizard.

Where to find it: Fonts and Font wizard sections.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Rounded / ChunkySoft, friendly shapes.Early years, primary school, short headings.
Serif / Sans serifWith or without small finishing strokes.Serif for an editorial tone; sans serif for clarity and signs.
HandwritingImitates handwriting or script.Invitations and decorative headings; avoid long text if readability is low.
Native outlineFonts already designed as outlines.Colouring sheets and hollow letters.
WizardSuggests fonts based on chosen shape, tone, and readability.When you do not know a typeface name.

How to use it

  1. Select text or choose the font before adding it.
  2. Filter by category or type a characteristic in search.
  3. Preview it with wording similar to your project.
  4. Apply the font and check easily confused characters such as I/l, a/o, and 1/7.
Recommended choices

For instructions and longer text, prefer simple typefaces. Reserve highly decorative fonts for headings. A font may need internet the first time.

Guided example
Early-years heading
Goal
Find a cheerful but readable typeface.
Steps
  1. Select the heading.
  2. Open Fonts and choose Rounded.
  3. Preview two or three fonts with the real word.
  4. Choose the one with the clearest letter shapes.
Expected result
A heading suited to the children’s age and easy to read.
Try next
Create an outline copy for a colouring version.
Continue with:Colours and outlinesAdding text

Fill, outline, and colour

Text and shapes can be filled, hollow with an outline, or combine fill and border. The result stays crisp when resized.

Where to find it: Colour and thickness controls in Text, Shapes, and outline Emoji sections.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
FillColours the inside.Normal text, filled shapes, and pictograms.
OutlineLeaves the inside empty and draws the border.Colouring letters, silhouettes, and light headings.
ThicknessAdjusts how strong the outline appears.Increase it for large prints or younger children.
EyedropperPicks a visible colour from the canvas.To coordinate text, shapes, and images.

How to use it

  1. Select the object to edit.
  2. Choose whether it should be filled or outlined.
  3. Set colour and thickness while watching the page.
  4. To reuse an existing colour, enable the eyedropper and select that point on the canvas.
Recommended choices

An outline that is too thin may disappear in print; one that is too thick may close internal letter spaces. Check at Fit and print a sample when precision matters.

Guided example
Colour-in name
Goal
Create a name with a white interior and black outline.
Steps
  1. Add the name using a wide font.
  2. Enable Outline and choose black.
  3. Increase thickness until the border is clear.
  4. Export a 150 dpi PDF test.
Expected result
Large letters that children can colour.
Try next
Add a light frame using an outline rectangle.
Continue with:Choosing a suitable fontPreparing print

Emoji and Clipart

OpenMoji offers consistent searchable symbols; Clipart searches illustrations published on Openclipart. Both make concepts, routines, and instructions immediate.

Where to find it: Emoji and Clipart sections in the panel.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Emoji categoriesFilter emotions, people, animals, food, symbols, and more.When browsing without a precise keyword.
Colour / OutlineChooses coloured or editable outline emoji.Colour for immediate use; outline for coordination or colouring.
Search translationHelps search in English from Italian words.Keep it enabled in Italian; press the search icon to start.
Clipart previewShows a larger image before inserting it.To check style, detail, and relevance.
Insert with PuterHelps when direct download fails.Only when signed in and willing to use Puter bandwidth or allowance.

How to use it

•Emoji / Clipart→•Search→•Preview→•Insert
  1. Choose a category or type a concrete word such as school, heart, or lion.
  2. Start the search with Enter or the search icon.
  3. Open the preview and insert the result on the page.
  4. Resize from corners; for outline emoji, adjust colour and thickness.
Recommended choices

Use images with a similar style on one page. Simple searches work better than long phrases. Always check that Clipart suits the classroom context.

Guided example
Emotion chart
Goal
Match words with recognisable symbols.
Steps
  1. Search happy, sad, angry, and surprised in Emoji.
  2. Insert the four faces.
  3. Add a word below each one.
  4. Use Align and Equal spacing to arrange them.
Expected result
A visual chart for routines and emotional conversations.
Try next
Duplicate the page and replace the words with questions or situations.
Continue with:Aligning elementsGrouping symbol and word

Shapes, arrows, and free drawing

Shapes are editable elements: you can change colour, border, size, and points. The collection includes geometry, school silhouettes, arrows, callouts, and drawing tools.

Where to find it: Shapes and drawing section.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
BasicRectangle, circle, triangle, star, and other geometry.Frames, labels, diagrams, and mathematics.
SchoolBooks, pencils, boards, globes, and classroom silhouettes.Worksheets and classroom signs.
ArrowsFilled, outline, double, and vertical arrows.Sequences, maps, and instructions.
Polygon / PolylineCreates a shape using points you choose.Custom diagrams and irregular outlines.
Freehand / Smooth freehandDraws a free stroke; the smooth version reduces wobble.Connections, signatures, circles, and annotations.
1:1Forces regular squares and circles while drawing.When width and height must match.

How to use it

•Shapes→▭Choose shape→•Drag on page→▧Select
  1. Choose category, shape, fill, outline, and thickness.
  2. Drag on the page to set its size.
  3. After insertion, you automatically return to selection to move or resize it.
  4. For vertex-based shapes, enable Edit points and drag nodes; disable the mode when finished.
Recommended choices

Existing objects are protected while drawing. On touch devices, polygons and polylines are easier with Drag to create segments. Escape cancels the current gesture.

Guided example
An illustrated sequence
Goal
Create three steps connected by arrows.
Steps
  1. Insert three rectangles with the same colour.
  2. Add a word or image to each.
  3. Choose an arrow and draw it between the boxes.
  4. Use Equal spacing to make the sequence regular.
Expected result
A clear, ordered visual procedure.
Try next
Duplicate the page to create another routine with the same spacing.
Continue with:Snapping and equal spacingGroups and layers

Groups, copy, and layers

Grouping makes a composition easier to move. Layers decide which object appears in front when items overlap.

Where to find it: Toolbar, object context menu, and Move up/down controls.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Group / UngroupCombines several items or separates them again.For decorated headings, labels, and repeated compositions.
Copy / PasteDuplicates editable items across pages and projects.To reuse a style or composition.
DuplicateCreates a copy near the original.When working on the same page.
Move up / downMoves by one layer.For small stacking corrections.
Move to top / bottomMoves directly in front of or behind everything.For backgrounds, frames, or elements that must dominate.
Duplicate as imageCreates a raster copy while retaining the editable original.For crop, image effects, or AI reference.

How to use it

  1. Select the items to treat together.
  2. Choose Group or Ctrl+G.
  3. Move, resize, or duplicate the group.
  4. If an item is hidden, use layer commands; use Ungroup when only one part needs editing.
Recommended choices

Group only after arranging the composition. A background should be moved to the bottom and then locked to prevent accidental movement.

Guided example
Reusable label
Goal
Create a label made of a shape, icon, and text.
Steps
  1. Insert a rounded rectangle.
  2. Add an emoji and a word.
  3. Select all three and group them.
  4. Copy and paste the group, then change only the word and emoji.
Expected result
A consistent set of labels that are easy to move.
Try next
Move each label to a different page using copy and paste.
Continue with:Multiple selectionContext menusDuplicate as image
🖼️

3. Work with images and photographs

Import, crop, optimise, and transform images while keeping print quality and device memory in mind.

Load images, PDFs, and clipboard content

You can start from a file, a copied image, a web address, a PDF, or Clipart. After insertion, the image becomes part of the project.

Where to find it: Images & Crop section.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Upload imageChooses a file from the device.Most reliable method for saved photos and illustrations.
Paste imageReads an image from the clipboard.After Copy image in a browser or another app.
From URLLoads a direct link to an image file.When you have the image address, not the web page address.
Use Puter to downloadUses Puter transport if direct loading is blocked.Only by explicit choice with a connected account; it may use allowance or bandwidth.
Import PDF as imagesTurns one or all PDF pages into chicCanva pages.For annotating handouts, worksheets, and existing resources.

How to use it

•Images→•Upload image→▧Select→⌗Crop
  1. Choose the most direct available source.
  2. Wait until the image appears on the page before changing page.
  3. Resize from corners and use Lock position if it becomes a background.
  4. Check Image information when print quality matters.
Recommended choices

For PDF, 1× is light, 2× is the normal choice, and 3× is useful only for fine detail. Import creates images: original PDF text does not become editable.

Guided example
Annotate a PDF worksheet
Goal
Import a page and add coloured directions.
Steps
  1. Choose Import PDF as images.
  2. Select one page, New project, and 2× quality.
  3. Add arrows, shapes, and text over the image.
  4. Export the page as PDF.
Expected result
A new annotated worksheet while the original PDF remains unchanged.
Try next
Duplicate the page for student and answer versions.
Continue with:Crop and qualityUsing an image as background

Crop, resolution, and image size

Crop shows only part of a photograph without deleting the original. Change quality alters pixel count or optimises the PNG while keeping its page size unchanged.

Where to find it: Images & Crop section with one image selected.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Crop modeOpens an adjustable frame over the visible area.To remove borders or focus on the subject.
Reset cropRestores the whole image.When changing framing without reloading the file.
0.25×–0.75×Reduces pixels and especially memory use.For very large photos used small on the page.
1×Keeps resolution and changes only PNG optimisation.When sharpness is right but the project is too large.
1.25×–4×Increases pixel count through interpolation.Only for compatibility or a source that is too small; it does not create real new detail.
PNG qualityReduces colour precision while retaining PNG and transparency.Lower gradually and check text, gradients, and skin tones.

How to use it

▧Select image→•Change quality→•Resolution→•Replace image
  1. For crop, choose Crop mode, adjust edges and position, and confirm.
  2. To optimise, open Change quality and review pixels, estimated memory, and DPI.
  3. Choose scale first, then PNG quality.
  4. Confirm Replace image and use Undo if the result is unsatisfactory.
Recommended choices

Reducing an enormous photo is often more useful than compressing it. In print, the larger the image on the page, the more pixels it needs. If it contains small text, inspect it at 100% after resizing.

Guided example
Optimise a photograph
Goal
Reduce memory use without changing its size on the worksheet.
Steps
  1. Select the photo and read DPI and estimated memory.
  2. Open Change quality and try 0.5×.
  3. Keep PNG quality high for the first attempt.
  4. Replace and compare details.
Expected result
The photo uses less memory but stays in the same position and size.
Try next
If still oversized, try 0.33×; if defects appear, undo and use 0.75×.
Continue with:Image effectsExport DPI

Black and white, outline, and raster copy

Local effects create a copy so you can compare it with the original. They are useful for colouring sheets, economical printing, and high-contrast resources.

Where to find it: Images & Crop section, effects block.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Black and whiteCreates a greyscale or stronger monochrome version.Photos to print without colour.
SoftnessMoves from strong edges to more photographic tones.Low for drawings; high for portraits and photos.
Image outlineExtracts edges on a light background.To obtain a colouring base without AI.
Duplicate as imageConverts text, a shape, or a group into transparent PNG.To apply crop, effects, or use the composition as an AI reference.

How to use it

  1. Select the image or composition.
  2. Choose the effect and adjust its visible parameter.
  3. Create the copy and move it next to the original for comparison.
  4. Keep only the useful version once you are satisfied.
Recommended choices

Outline works best with subjects clearly separated from the background. For complex photos, the AI Colouring page workflow may work better.

Guided example
Economical photo printing
Goal
Prepare a clear photo for a black-and-white printer.
Steps
  1. Select the photo and create a Black and white copy.
  2. Adjust softness to preserve faces and details.
  3. Export a 150 dpi test page.
  4. Increase contrast only if the print looks flat.
Expected result
A photograph that remains readable without colour.
Try next
Add a thin border and caption to separate it from the background.
Continue with:ColorizerAI colouring page

Remove a background

You can remove a uniform background with a quick local method or use a more advanced local model for photographs and complex edges.

Where to find it: Images & Crop section, Remove background box.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Uniform backgroundMakes pixels similar to a chosen colour transparent.Clipart, scans, and generated images with a flat background.
Detect from edgesAutomatically estimates the background colour.When the background clearly surrounds the subject.
ToleranceControls how different removed colours may be.Increase if halos remain; reduce if subject parts disappear.
Internal areasAlso removes matching areas not connected to the edge.Disable if the subject contains the background colour.
Local AIRecognises the subject without sending the photo to a remote service.People, hair, animals, and varied backgrounds.

How to use it

▧Select image→•Remove background→•Method→Duplicate without background
  1. Duplicate the image if you want a visible comparison.
  2. Try Uniform background first when the colour is flat.
  3. Use the eyedropper or automatic detection and adjust tolerance.
  4. Use local AI removal only for complex edges; first use may need to download the model.
Recommended choices

The uniform method is fast and predictable. Local AI needs more memory and time but handles hair and photographs better. Both create a copy and do not consume Puter generation credits.

Guided example
Cut out clipart on white
Goal
Create a transparent subject to place over a coloured shape.
Steps
  1. Select the clipart.
  2. Choose Uniform background and Detect from edges.
  3. Check that important internal white areas remain visible.
  4. Create the copy and place it over the shape.
Expected result
The subject appears without a white box.
Try next
Add a subtle shadow shape behind the subject for contrast.
Continue with:AI post-processingManaging layers

Colorizer: colour closed areas

Colorizer temporarily turns a selection into a colourable surface. You can fill areas, use a brush, and later change colours, gradients, or textures.

Where to find it: Colorizer section; first select an image, text, shape, or group.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Quality 1×–4×Sets detail when the object is converted.2× is the normal balance; 1× for low-memory devices.
FillColours a connected area with one tap.For spaces enclosed by closed outlines.
Smart brushPaints without easily crossing the starting boundary.For small gaps, details, and corrections.
Do not cross edgesKeeps strokes within detected boundaries.Keep it enabled in most cases.
Solid / Gradient / TextureChooses the region appearance.Solid for clarity; gradient or texture for decoration.
Restore originalReturns to editable elements from before conversion.When source text, shapes, or groups need correction.

How to use it

  1. Select the subject and choose Start Colorizer.
  2. Choose Fill and tap a closed area.
  3. If colour escapes, undo, reduce Tolerance, or close the gap with the brush.
  4. Choose Finish mode when you want to move or resize the object again.
Recommended choices

Use pinch to reach details: the gesture does not apply colour. Keep a copy of the result before Restore original if you want both versions.

Guided example
Colour an outline house
Goal
Fill roof, windows, and door with different colours.
Steps
  1. Select the house and start Colorizer at 2×.
  2. Fill closed areas with solid colours.
  3. Use the smart brush to close small gaps.
  4. Finish the mode and copy the result.
Expected result
A coloured house with visible outlines.
Try next
Duplicate the image to try a second palette without losing the first.
Continue with:Creating an outline baseZoom and pinch
✨

4. Use AI with confidence

Understand what you are asking, which model to choose, what it may cost, and how to guide the result with prompts and references.

What Puter and AI models are

Puter is the connected service that lets chicCanva use several image generators through the user’s account. An AI model is the system that interprets the prompt and produces the image: different models may have different costs, controls, and strengths.

Where to find it: AI image generation · Puter section.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Sign in with PuterConnects the account required for AI and assisted downloads.Only when you decide to use these features.
Family / providerGroups models by originating service.Use it to narrow the model menu.
ModelChooses the generator that receives the request.Based on precision, available controls, style, and cost.
Switch account / Sign outSelects another account or ends the session.On shared devices or before leaving the computer.

How to use it

  1. Choose Sign in with Puter and complete the official service window.
  2. Check the account name shown in the section.
  3. Read available credit and the estimate before generating.
  4. Choose Generate only when the prompt and settings are ready.
Recommended choices

Simply opening the section does not generate images or start charges. A request begins only with Generate and insert. Prompts and reference images are sent to the model selected at that moment.

Guided example
First controlled generation
Goal
Try AI with a simple task and an economical setting.
Steps
  1. Sign in and check the balance.
  2. Choose GPT Image 2.5 Flare, Low, 1:1, and 1K.
  3. Write a simple prompt without a reference.
  4. Check the estimate and choose Generate once.
Expected result
A first image inserted on the page, with usage visible after the request.
Try next
Save the successful prompt in Prompt Library and change one thing at a time.
Continue with:Writing a promptComparing modelsUnderstanding cost

Write an effective prompt

A prompt is the description you give the model. There are no magic formulas: concrete, ordered requests that match the teaching purpose work best.

Where to find it: Prompt field, Illustration style preset, and Prompt Library in the AI section.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
SubjectStates what should appear.Always start here: a fox, three children, a map.
Action and contextDefines what happens and where.To avoid generic images.
StyleGuides technique, colours, and realism.Use presets as a starting point, then state important details.
ConstraintsStates quantity, composition, and what must not appear.When the resource must meet a precise brief.
Visible textRequests words inside the image.Write the exact wording and language; always check generated spelling.
Prompt LibrarySaves prompts, tags, description, style, and optional reference.For recurring creative instructions and activity templates.

How to use it

•AI→•Choose model→•Write prompt→•Generate and insert
  1. First write subject and action in a simple sentence.
  2. Add audience and purpose, such as children aged 6 or a colouring worksheet.
  3. Specify composition, colours, background, and required details.
  4. Choose a preset and open Show full prompt sent to review what will be added.
Recommended choices

Ask for one main thing at a time. To correct a result, describe the desired difference instead of rewriting everything. For visible text, state words and language manually: chicCanva does not add an automatic language rule.

Guided example
Classroom-rule illustration
Goal
Create a clear scene for the rule Raise your hand.
Steps
  1. Write: A primary classroom, one child raises a hand, classmates seated and attentive.
  2. Add: simple illustration, light background, few details, space at the top for a heading.
  3. Choose Educational clipart or Clean cartoon.
  4. Generate and add text with chicCanva instead of asking the model.
Expected result
A readable scene to which you can add a correct, editable heading.
Try next
Save the prompt and change only the action to create a consistent rule series.
Continue with:Choosing a modelUsing a reference

Which model to choose

There is no single best model for every task. The choice depends on budget, required control, and whether you need to edit a reference image.

Where to find it: Family / provider and Model menus in the AI section.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
GPT Image 2.5 FlareOffers Low, Medium, High, flexible sizes, references, and annotations.First drafts, classroom illustrations, colouring pages, and cost-conscious work.
GPT Image 2.5 SunburstHas the same controls and favours more precise targeted edits.When annotating a reference or changing a specific area.
GPT Image 2OpenAI generation with Low and Medium and size controls.Compatibility with a simpler OpenAI workflow.
Grok Imagine StandardxAI option with 1K and 2K levels.To compare an alternative interpretation at lower cost than Quality.
Grok Imagine QualityxAI variant aimed at a more refined result.When willing to spend more credit on one refined attempt.
Seedream 5 LiteAlternative model with simple settings and per-image price.To explore a different aesthetic without many parameters.
Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image1K output, many aspect ratios, and reference support.For quick trials, varied formats, and reference-based edits.

How to use it

  1. Start with Flare Low when you do not yet have a target result.
  2. Move to Sunburst when changing areas indicated by markers.
  3. Try another family when you want a different interpretation or its specific controls.
  4. Compare results using the same prompt and changing one variable only.
Recommended choices

Model names and availability belong to connected services and may change over time. chicCanva shows curated combinations only; if a model fails, it is not silently replaced by another paid model.

Guided example
Draft and final version
Goal
Reduce waste while exploring.
Steps
  1. Generate with Flare Low and 1K.
  2. Refine the prompt until composition and subjects are right.
  3. Only then move to Medium, High, or a more precise model.
  4. Keep the final prompt in the library.
Expected result
Fewer expensive attempts and a more informed final choice.
Try next
Save a prompt variant for a different style or age group.
Continue with:Quality, size, and costTargeted annotations

Quality, resolution, aspect ratio, and usage

Quality and resolution are not the same. Quality indicates how much work the model performs; resolution indicates how many pixels the image contains. Both may affect usage.

Where to find it: Controls below the model and the Estimated usage box.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
LowMore economical generation suited to drafts.First draft, ideas, simple colouring pages.
MediumMore refinement at an intermediate cost.When the composition is already established.
HighHighest available level for models that offer it.Final result or difficult details; avoid it for casual trials.
Aspect ratioDefines shape: square, landscape, or portrait.Choose it for the real space on the page.
Short side / 1K / 2KDetermines pixel count.1K for normal use; 1.5K–2K for larger print or cropping.
Custom dimensionsAllows exact width and height in compatible models.Only when you know the required size; chicCanva corrects invalid combinations.
Estimate / Last GenCompares forecast with observed usage of the last similar request.Read them before and after generation.

How to use it

  1. First choose the ratio for the destination: 1:1 for cards, 4:3 for landscape resources, 3:4 or 9:16 for portrait.
  2. Use Low and around 1K for a draft.
  3. Check Estimated usage and available credit.
  4. Increase quality or resolution only when you know which result you want to keep.
Recommended choices

The estimate is indicative; the balance reported by Puter after the request is authoritative. A reference image, especially a large one, may increase usage. Annotations send two same-sized images and the estimate accounts for both.

Guided example
Image for an A4 worksheet
Goal
Create a clear illustration without immediately using maximum quality.
Steps
  1. Choose a ratio similar to the space available on the worksheet.
  2. Generate a Low 1K draft.
  3. Insert it and check size and composition.
  4. If it is right, repeat at 1.5K or Medium.
Expected result
A two-stage process that limits expensive attempts.
Try next
Reuse the same aspect ratio to keep later pages consistent.
Continue with:Puter creditModel choice

Use a reference image

A reference shows the model what to retain: subject, pose, colours, composition, or style. It does not guarantee an identical copy, but makes the request more concrete.

Where to find it: Optional reference image box in the AI section.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
From URL / Attach / PasteLoads the reference from different sources.Use the most direct and reliable available method.
From canvasUses the visible part of the selected image.To transform or reinterpret an item already in the project.
0.25× / 0.5× / 0.75×Sends a smaller copy.To reduce usage when overall shape and colours are enough.
1×Sends the current reference dimensions.Default and normally recommended.
2× / 3×Sends a larger copy.Only when small details truly matter; it may increase cost and time.

How to use it

  1. Load the reference and inspect the preview.
  2. Keep 1× for the first attempt.
  3. In the prompt, explicitly state what to retain and what to change.
  4. Remove or replace the reference when starting a different task.
Recommended choices

Do not rely on the image alone: write ‘keep the pose and colours, change the background’. A clean, well-cropped reference is more useful than an enormous, cluttered image.

Guided example
Turn a photo into an illustration
Goal
Keep the subject while making the style more suitable for a worksheet.
Steps
  1. Select the photo on canvas and choose From canvas.
  2. Keep scale at 1×.
  3. State what must remain recognisable and choose an illustration preset.
  4. Generate a Low draft.
Expected result
A new image inspired by the photo, inserted beside the original.
Try next
If one area needs a precise change, use annotations.
Continue with:Annotating the referenceDescribing what to retain

Annotate a reference for targeted edits

With GPT Image 2.5, you can draw numbered markers over a reference copy and attach a comment to each. The model receives both the clean and annotated images.

Where to find it: Annotate reference image button, available after loading a reference and choosing Flare or Sunburst.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
SelectMoves, resizes, or edits an existing marker.After drawing; Spot does not resize.
RectangleMarks an area with regular boundaries.Objects, writing, furniture, and rectangular areas.
OvalHighlights a soft area or subject.Faces, heads, patches, and circular elements.
SpotMarks a precise point with a numbered dot.Small details, a part’s colour, or insertion point.
Comment panelWrites the edit associated with the selected marker.Opens automatically after a new marker.
Delete / Delete allRemoves the selected marker; right-click or long press shows delete all.Always check the number before deleting.

How to use it

•Reference image→▭Annotate→•Write comment→•Save annotations
  1. Choose Annotate reference image and use zoom or pinch to reach the detail.
  2. Draw a Rectangle, Oval, or Spot; the tool automatically returns to Select.
  3. In the panel, write a self-contained precise instruction such as Make the shirt dark green.
  4. Save annotations, inspect the full prompt, and preferably generate with Sunburst for targeted edits.
Recommended choices

A marker should contain only what it describes. Avoid vague comments such as ‘fix this’: state the action, colour, or replacement. Changing model keeps annotations but an incompatible model disables them; changing reference clears them.

Guided example
Change two details in a room
Goal
Change a lamp and sofa while leaving the rest unchanged.
Steps
  1. Place a Spot on the lamp and write Make it matte black.
  2. Draw a Rectangle over the sofa and write Replace with a dark-blue sofa.
  3. Save and choose Sunburst.
  4. In the main prompt, ask to preserve the room, perspective, and lighting.
Expected result
An edit guided by numbered markers, with the rest of the scene more stable.
Try next
If too much changes, reinforce in the prompt what must stay unchanged.
Continue with:Reference imageFlare and Sunburst

Generate, insert, and recover the result

Generate and insert starts an explicit request. If the image is created but the browser cannot insert it, chicCanva keeps a temporary preview with recovery actions.

Where to find it: Bottom of the AI section, below Estimated usage.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Generate and insertSends prompt, settings, and references and inserts the result.When everything is checked and you accept the estimated usage.
Chroma keyRequests a flat background very different from the subject.When you want easy background removal after generation.
Duplicate and remove backgroundAfter generation, creates a second locally background-removed copy.When you want both the original and a transparent subject.
Retry insertionRetries importing an already generated result.Does not start another generation or repay the model.
Download / OpenSaves or opens a recovered result.When canvas insertion keeps failing.

How to use it

  1. Check full prompt, model, format, reference, and estimate.
  2. Choose Generate and wait without clicking again.
  3. If the recovery preview appears, try Retry insertion first.
  4. Download the result before closing or refreshing if insertion fails.
Recommended choices

An insertion error does not necessarily mean generation failed. Use actions on the existing preview: starting a new request may consume more credit.

Guided example
Create a transparent character
Goal
Generate a subject for use over different backgrounds.
Steps
  1. Describe one full character and choose a simple style.
  2. Enable Chroma key and Duplicate generated content and remove background.
  3. Generate at Low quality for the draft.
  4. Keep the transparent copy and place it over a coloured shape.
Expected result
Original and transparent copy available in the same project.
Try next
Copy the character to several pages and change only background and caption.
Continue with:Local background removalSaving the result

Prepare an AI colouring page

Prepare colouring image with AI configures model, quality, style, reference, and a starting prompt. It does not generate automatically: you can review and edit everything first.

Where to find it: Image effects, with a photo or image selected.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Age and difficultyAdjusts the amount and size of detail.State, for example, ages 5–6 or primary school.
Closed outlinesMakes hand colouring or Colorizer easier.Always request them for a colouring worksheet.
White background, no shadingAvoids greys and textures that are hard to print.For photocopying and economical print.
Recognisable featuresStates what must remain faithful to the reference.Pose, proportions, clothing, or important objects.

How to use it

  1. Select the photo or subject and choose Prepare colouring image with AI.
  2. Open the AI section and check the reference, Flare Low, and Colouring page preset.
  3. Add age, details to retain, and desired simplicity.
  4. Generate, inspect outlines, and retry with fewer details if they are too complex.
Recommended choices

Low is often enough for the first version. If the subject is not recognisable, improve the prompt or crop the reference better; increasing quality alone does not always fix an unclear request.

Guided example
Animal colouring page
Goal
Turn a photograph into a simple children’s worksheet.
Steps
  1. Select a photo with the animal clearly visible.
  2. Choose Prepare colouring image with AI.
  3. Add: for children aged 6, large areas, few background details.
  4. Generate Low and print a test.
Expected result
A black-and-white drawing with large areas and a recognisable subject.
Try next
Add the animal name and a short instruction using Text tools.
Continue with:Colouring digitallyImproving the prompt
📐

5. Refine, review, and export

Align precisely, review every page, and choose the right format for print, sharing, or future editing.

Grid, snapping, guides, and fitting

These aids keep a composition orderly but are not printed. You can use a regular grid or magnetic guides that appear near edges, centres, and equal gaps.

Where to find it: Canvas, grid and snap section and the Snap icon context menu.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Grid mmShows a grid with a physical step.For diagrams, labels, and repeatable measurements.
Classic snapMoves objects to configured intervals.When you want regular numeric positions.
Page centre / edgesAttracts selection to page centre and edges.Centred headings, backgrounds, and frames.
Align to objectsCompares edges and centres of other items.For ordered rows and columns.
Equal spacingShows when gaps between objects match.Flashcards, image grids, and visual tables.
Fit with / without marginCentres and scales selection with or without a margin.With margin for content; without margin for full-page backgrounds and images.

How to use it

  1. Enable only the aids needed for the current task.
  2. Drag slowly near the target and watch the coloured lines.
  3. Release when the indicated centre, edge, or spacing is correct.
  4. To fill the page, open Fit selection from the object menu and choose the margin.
Recommended choices

Alt temporarily reverses guides while moving; Shift + Alt excludes them and reverses classic snap. These shortcuts do not change saved settings.

Guided example
Four evenly spaced images
Goal
Create an ordered row without manual measurement.
Steps
  1. Insert and resize four images.
  2. Enable Align to objects and Equal spacing.
  3. First align vertical centres.
  4. Move inner images until equal-gap guidance appears.
Expected result
A regular row ready for labels or captions.
Try next
Group the row and fit it to width with a margin.
Continue with:Multiple selectionGrouping the composition

Preview and project review

Preview shows all pages together. Use it to check order, consistency, orientation, and empty pages before export.

Where to find it: Preview button in the top bar.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Thumbnail sizeEnlarges or reduces previews.Small for overall order; large for detail checks.
ReorderEnables page movement.Before multi-page export.
Arrows / dragMoves the selected page.Arrows on touch; dragging on desktop.
Click thumbnailCloses Preview and opens that page.When you find something to correct.

How to use it

▦Preview→•Review pages→•Reorder→•Open page
  1. Open Preview after completing a first version of all pages.
  2. Reduce thumbnails to check order and visual rhythm.
  3. Enlarge them to find empty pages, inconsistent headings, or wrong orientation.
  4. Open the page to correct and return to Preview afterwards.
Recommended choices

Thumbnails are lightweight and may look less sharp than final export. Judge composition and order; use the canvas for fine details.

Guided example
Final booklet review
Goal
Find mistakes before creating the PDF.
Steps
  1. Open Preview and count pages.
  2. Check cover, activities, and answers are in the right order.
  3. Check headings and margins are consistent.
  4. Open and correct each issue, then review again.
Expected result
An ordered project before final export.
Try next
Ask someone to check one sample page before printing everything.
Continue with:Exporting the projectReordering pages

Choose PDF, PNG, JPG, ZIP, and JSON

The format depends on what happens next. PDF is for pages and print; PNG and JPG are images; JSON preserves the editable project.

Where to find it: Export centre in the panel and PDF/JSON shortcuts in the top bar.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
PDFKeeps page sizes and orientations in one document.Print, sharing with colleagues, and multi-page projects.
PNGCrisp image with optional transparency.Graphics, slides, web, clipboard, and transparent resources.
JPGSmaller image with white background and adjustable quality.Photographs and sharing when transparency is unnecessary.
ZIPCollects one separate image for each page.When exporting every page as PNG or JPG.
JSONSaves pages, objects, and images in editable form.Backup, transfer, and future work.
Copy to clipboardCopies one page or area as an image without immediately creating a file.To paste into presentations, messages, or AI reference.

How to use it

•Export→•What to export→•Format→•Export
  1. Choose what to export: all pages, current page, or selection.
  2. Choose the format for the destination.
  3. Set DPI, quality, and background when available.
  4. Read the final button label: it describes the result that will be created.
Recommended choices

150 dpi suits drafts and everyday printing; 300 dpi suits more detailed final print. PNG is preferable for text, outlines, and transparency. JPG at 85–92% is often a good compromise for photos. Always keep JSON if you may edit the work.

Guided example
Deliver a worksheet and keep its source
Goal
Create one file for printing and one for future editing.
Steps
  1. Review the page in Preview.
  2. Export a 300 dpi PDF for the final version.
  3. Also export JSON without history for a smaller file.
  4. Open the PDF and inspect a page before sharing.
Expected result
A ready-to-use PDF and a project that can be reopened.
Try next
Keep PDF and JSON in the same folder with recognisable names.
Continue with:Backup and recoveryImage quality

Share files and transfer projects

chicCanva can open the device Share menu, receive files in the installed PWA, and transfer projects directly between two devices that are open at the same time.

Where to find it: Share icons, when supported for the selected format, in the Export centre and Prompt Library; P2P Project Sharing below Import/Export JSON.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Share fileCreates the same PDF, PNG, JPG, ZIP, or JSON as export and opens the system share sheet.For quickly sending to a compatible app without first finding the file in Downloads.
PWA as a share targetThe installed PWA can receive PDFs, projects, Prompt Libraries, and images shared from other apps.When you choose chicCanva from Share in Telegram, Files, or Gallery.
Send P2PShows a QR and one-time code for selected projects and the Prompt Library.For moving work between a computer, tablet, or phone without uploading it to cloud storage.
Receive P2PReads the QR or code, shows the list, and imports only checked items.When both devices have chicCanva open and are online.
Append Prompt LibraryKeeps existing prompts; optionally replaces prompts with the same name.For combining collections from several devices or colleagues.
Replace Prompt LibraryReplaces the whole library after confirmation.For restoring a complete, known backup.

How to use it

•Export→•Share / P2P→•QR or code→•Choose and import
  1. For a ready file, choose format and options in the Export centre. If the device accepts that file type, the small Share icon appears; otherwise use Export.
  2. For direct transfer, open P2P Project Sharing on the sending device and select the content.
  3. On the second device choose Receive, then scan the QR or enter the code.
  4. Review the received list, choose the items, and confirm import.
Recommended choices

Share availability also depends on the format: the same browser may accept PDFs and images but not JSON or ZIP. Export always remains available. The P2P code is temporary and should be shared only with the recipient; very restrictive school networks may block the connection.

Guided example
Move a workshop from computer to tablet
Goal
Transfer two projects and the prompts used without sending several attachments.
Steps
  1. On the computer open P2P Project Sharing and select the two projects plus Prompt Library.
  2. Choose Create code and wait.
  3. On the tablet open Receive and scan the QR.
  4. Check the two projects, choose Add for Prompt Library, and start receiving.
Expected result
The tablet shows separate new projects and adds the prompts to its existing collection.
Try next
Open a received project, check the fonts, and also create a final PDF.
Continue with:Choosing a formatKeeping a backupInstalling the PWA

Use chicCanva on phone and tablet

On small screens, the panel temporarily overlays part of the canvas, bars scroll horizontally, and handles are larger. Features and project format remain the same.

Where to find it: Automatic mobile layout and installable PWA from Install when available.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Open / Close panelSwitches between tools and workspace.Open to choose, close to compose.
PinchZooms and pans the page with two fingers without moving objects.For details and navigation.
Long pressOpens context menus for objects, pages, and tools.Equivalent to right-click.
Tap selectionSelects several items with successive taps.When Ctrl is unavailable or objects overlap.
InstallAdds chicCanva to the app screen and enables PWA launch.On an HTTPS domain and compatible browser.

How to use it

  1. Open the panel, choose the tool, and close it.
  2. Use two fingers to reach the relevant point.
  3. For several objects, open the Selection menu and start Tap selection.
  4. Scroll projects and toolbar horizontally to reach the final buttons.
Recommended choices

On low-memory devices, reduce enormous images and use moderate AI quality. Keep autosave enabled and export JSON after important sessions.

Guided example
Compose a worksheet on a tablet
Goal
Use all available space without losing controls.
Steps
  1. Open the panel and insert text and an image.
  2. Close the panel and use pinch to position them.
  3. Start Tap selection to select them together.

A worksheet composed without accidental dragging during pinch.

Install the PWA to reopen the workspace more quickly.

6. Creative workshop

Four complete workflows show how to combine tools for real classroom activities. Use them as a starting point and adapt them to your class.

Welcome poster

An effective poster guides the eye with a heading, a few visual elements, and a message readable from a distance.

Where to find it: Combine Text, Fonts, Emoji or Clipart, Shapes, Snap, and Export.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Portrait formatMakes room for a heading, image, and message in a column.Doors, corridors, and noticeboards.
Large headingMakes the main message immediate.A short phrase with strong contrast.
Single imageKeeps the composition from becoming crowded.Choose a recognisable symbol or a consistent AI illustration.

How to use it

  1. Create a portrait page and choose a light background colour.
  2. Add the heading, try two fonts, and keep the more readable one.
  3. Insert one central image and a short welcome sentence.
  4. Centre the content, review it in Preview, and export a 300 dpi PDF.
Recommended choices

View the poster at 50%: if the heading remains readable, the hierarchy works. Limit fonts to two and use the brightest colour for one important element.

Guided example
Welcome to our class
Goal
Prepare an A4 poster for the first day.
Steps
  1. Write Welcome to our class.
  2. Insert a sun or a group of children.
  3. Add the class name at the bottom.
  4. Export a 300 dpi PDF.

A clear, cheerful poster ready to print.
Try next
Duplicate the page and create versions for the library, laboratory, and gym.

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it

Guided example
Animal flashcards

Create eight consistent cards with an image and name.
Steps

Eight consistent cards that are easy to print and reorder.

Colouring worksheet

You can start from shapes, outline emoji, a simplified photograph, or an AI image, then prepare clear areas and readable outlines.

What is available

Outline emojiProvide clean, editable outlines.Simple subjects and symbols.

Guided example
Water cycle colouring page

Bilingual resources and visual routines

Consistent icons and short phrases help create routines that remain understandable while a language is still being learned.

Where to find it: Combine Text, Emoji/Clipart, groups, Duplicate page, and copy/paste.

What is available

OptionWhat it doesWhen to choose it
Two languages side by sideShows the correspondence immediately.Signs, rules, and vocabulary.
One language per pageKeeps graphics identical and reduces crowding.Differentiated worksheets or presentations.
Icon plus sentenceSupports understanding without replacing text.Routines, instructions, and independence.

How to use it

  1. Create a sample row with an icon and sentence in the first language.
  2. Duplicate the sentence or page and enter the second language.
  3. Check that longer text remains readable and aligned.
  4. Group each row and duplicate the structure for other routines.
Recommended choices

Keep icons, colours, and positions consistent across languages. Always check accents, punctuation, and reading direction with someone competent in the language.

Guided example
Morning routine
Goal
Create five visual instructions in Italian and English.
Steps
  1. Create the first row with icon, Italian, and English.
  2. Group the row.
  3. Duplicate it four times.
  4. Replace icons and sentences, then use Equal spacing.
Expected result
A consistent, readable bilingual sequence.
Try next
Duplicate the page and hide one language for a recall activity.
Continue with:Choosing clear symbolsAligning a sequence

🖱️ Context menus

Right-clicking, or pressing and holding on touch, opens actions related to the item you indicated. Items change according to what is selected; unavailable actions remain disabled or are not shown.

WhereActions
Object on the pageCopy, paste, group or ungroup, split text, lock position, duplicate, fit selection, move to top or bottom, crop, remove background, use as AI reference, duplicate as image, rotate and flip, delete.
Project tabRename, export JSON, close project.
PageRename, open page, duplicate page. Preview also includes reordering controls.
Copying an imageCopy the original image or only the visible crop.
Delete annotationIn the Annotations panel, right-clicking or pressing and holding Delete also offers Delete all annotations.

Useful words in plain language

Project
The container for your work: it includes one or more pages and every inserted item.
Page
One sheet in the project, with its own size and orientation.
Canvas
The central area where you compose the page.
Object
A selectable item such as text, image, shape, or group.
Group
Several objects joined so they can be moved and resized together.
Layer
The front-to-back position among overlapping objects.
Crop
The visible crop of an image; the original pixels remain available.
Transparency
Areas with no colour that reveal what lies underneath.
Pixel
The smallest point in a digital image. More pixels allow more detail but require more memory.
Resolution
The number of pixels available across width and height.
DPI
A print setting: for the same page size, higher values give more detail and larger files.
PNG
A crisp image format suited to text, outlines, and transparency.
JPG
A compressed image format, often smaller for photographs, without transparency.
PDF
A page-based document designed for printing and sharing.
JSON
The editable chicCanva file, useful for backup or continued work.
Prompt
The description or instruction you give an AI model.
AI model
The system that interprets the prompt and creates or edits the image; models differ in strengths and cost.
Reference image
An image sent to the model to indicate a subject, style, or items to edit.
Aspect ratio
The relationship between width and height, such as square 1:1 or landscape 16:9.
Puter credits
The unit shown by Puter to measure connected service usage; an estimate appears before generation.

Frequently asked questions

Where can I find a tool?

Use the categories at the top of the panel or this guide’s contents. On mobile, scroll horizontal bars and open the panel when needed.

Are the grid and guides printed?

No. They are visual canvas aids and are not included in export.

Does zoom change print quality?

No. Zoom only changes how large the page appears on screen. Quality and DPI are chosen during export.

Why does an image look blurred?

The source may have too few pixels or may be enlarged greatly. Check Image information and, if possible, use a larger source or Change quality.

Why does AI misspell words?

Image models also treat letters as shapes. For exact wording, generate the visual without text and add text with chicCanva tools.

Does every AI generation cost the same?

No. Model, quality, size, references, and number of results can change usage. Always check the estimate before choosing Generate.

Does background removal upload my image?

Integrated background removal runs locally in the browser. The first use may download the required model.

Are autosave and JSON the same?

No. Autosave remains in the current browser; JSON is a portable file you can archive and reopen elsewhere.

Can I work offline?

The PWA can reopen many local features after the first load. AI, online Clipart, Puter sign-in, and other network resources still require a connection.

Does text remain editable in the PDF?

PDF is intended as a final result for printing or sharing. Keep the JSON to edit text and objects in chicCanva.

What happens if a font is missing?

chicCanva tries to use an available font; appearance may change. For an important transfer, check the project on the destination device and also export a PDF.

How do I undo a crop?

Use Undo immediately after cropping, or reopen Crop and restore the full visible area when available for that image.

How do I prevent accidental movement on mobile?

Use two fingers to zoom and pan the page: during pinch, objects and active tools are protected. You can also lock finished items.

What if an AI result is ready but is not inserted?

Use the recovery actions shown in the panel, such as retry insertion, open, or download. Do not immediately start a new generation because it may use more credits.
